stimulus.text:
“We therefore beseech your Majesty, that your royal authority and influence may be graciously interposed to procure us relief from our afflicting fears and jealousies, occasioned by the system before-mentioned, and to settle peace through every part of our dominions, with all humility submitting to your Majesty’s wise consideration, whether it may not be expedient for facilitating those important purposes, that your Majesty be pleased to direct some mode, by which the united applications of your faithful Colonists to the throne, in presence of their Common Councils, may be improved into a happy and permanent reconciliation; and that in the mean time measures may be taken for preventing the further destruction of the lives of your Majesty’s subjects; and that such statutes as more immediately distress any of your Majesty’s Colonies may be repealed.”
—Olive Branch Petition, Second Continental Congress, July 5, 1775 (abridged)

books.section: Topic 3.5 The American Revolution, A. The War for Independence

stem: The petition failed to achieve its aim because King George III

options.text: Replaced it with a new charter for Massachusetts
options.misconception: The king offered no new charter; he answered the petition by declaring the colonies in rebellion in August 1775.

options.text: Refused to read it and declared the colonies in rebellion
Accepted it and repealed the Coercive Acts at once
options.misconception: The king did not accept the petition; he refused to read it and the Coercive Acts stayed in force.

options.text: Sent it to Parliament, which voted to grant independence
options.misconception: Parliament never voted to grant independence; the king treated the colonies as rebels and the war went on.

rationales.B: The king refused to receive the petition and, in August 1775, proclaimed the colonies in rebellion, closing the door on reconciliation.
rationales.C: The king did not accept the petition — he refused it, so the harsh statutes were not repealed.
rationales.D: No vote for independence came from Parliament; the king's answer was a proclamation of rebellion.
rationales.A: No new charter was offered; the Massachusetts Government Act stayed in place and the war continued.
rationales.general:
1. Read the ask again. Congress wants the king to step in, repeal the harsh laws, and settle a reconciliation.
2. Ask what the king did. He would not receive the petition and declared the colonies in rebellion.
3. Name the result. The last attempt at reconciliation failed, and the war Congress had tried to avoid went on.
Remember: a petition only works if the person addressed is willing to read it — refusal is itself an answer. Background: the king issued his Proclamation of Rebellion in August 1775.
